logline: A self-destructive corporate executive returns from a breakdown and rehab radiating spiritual resolve, then channels her erratic idealism into exposing the company that humiliated her.

renewal.note: HBO cancelled Enlightened in March 2013 after two seasons despite widespread critical acclaim, citing low viewership. Creator Mike White confirmed no revival plans.

bollymeter.basis: Metacritic season score of 74 from 29 critics reflects a divided but largely admiring reception; the Los Angeles Times called it the most interesting and ambitious series of the fall season.

pull_quotes.text: The most interesting and ambitious series of the fall season.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 of Enlightened introduced Amy Jellicoe mid-meltdown and dared viewers to follow her through the wreckage. Laura Dern's performance is the engine: raw, absurd, occasionally unwatchable in the best sense. Critics split on whether Amy's New Age resolve was satire or sincerity - a productive ambiguity Mike White exploited deliberately. Metacritic logged a 74 from 29 reviewers, classing it generally favorable, with the Los Angeles Times calling it the most interesting and ambitious series of the fall. HBO's half-hour format let episodes breathe like essays rather than plot delivery vehicles. The season's weakness was pace - its meditative drift occasionally tipped into stasis. But Dern's Golden Globe win confirmed that the performance cut through even when the drama didn't.

episode_reviews.title: Pilot
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Amy returns from a Hawaiian treatment center with a new vocabulary for herself and zero tolerance for the corporate world that broke her. The premiere is as much character study as comedy, and Dern makes Amy's conviction feel genuinely strange rather than charming.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Amy's voiceover narration signals the show's real subject: not workplace satire but the gap between who we want to be and who we keep being.

bollymeter.basis: Metacritic season score of 95 with near-universal acclaim; the Huffington Post called it one of the best stories experienced in a long time, and it stands as one of the highest-rated HBO seasons of the decade.

pull_quotes.text: The show's must-see second season is one of the best stories I've experienced in a long time.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 is the rare case where a show finds its sharpest form just before cancellation. Mike White constructed a coherent investigative arc around Amy's corporate whistleblowing, giving the season a momentum the first lacked. The Metacritic score leapt to 95, placing it among the year's critical consensus picks. New York Magazine cited a vision so much wider than other shows featuring flawed heroines. The eight-episode structure felt purposeful: every hour advances both the external plot and Amy's internal contradictions. The finale aired as a proper conclusion yet the show ended weeks later. Critics mourned the cancellation loudly. The Huffington Post called it must-see television. Season 2 alone is the argument for Enlightened as an HBO masterwork.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 delivers the investigative urgency Season 1 withheld, transforming Amy's ambient idealism into a specific whistleblower storyline that gives the show its best hours.

episode_reviews.title: The Ghost Is Seen
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves Amy's crusade with a quiet devastation - consequences land not with spectacle but with the specific texture of real institutional defeat and real personal change.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The story breaks public in a way Amy never quite controlled, leaving her changed and the corporation barely scratched - a conclusion as honest as television gets.
